catalog_quote: I have no explanation for the circumflex on final <â> in <tanâ> ‘egg’; it may eventually turn out to represent vowel length or nasality. If stress is indicated in the Nutabe (and Catío) data provided by Rivet, it is found on the final syllable throughout.

new_statements.check: reported by the second reader, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Both works were marked silent and both were spot-checked directly (a full-text search for stress/accent the three archive.org volumes; fresh FTS queries for stress/accent/prosody on the Adelaar & Muysken item). Nothing on stress or accent for Nutabé / Old Catío was found in either; the only stress passages the Adelaar & Muysken search surfaces belong to Cholón, Quechua I, Guajiro and the transcription conventions. Rivet 1943 (earlier reading, pp. 25-39) also has no 'accent'/'tonique'. No missed statement.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: hdl.handle.net/1887/67094 resolves (302 -> scholarlypublications.universiteitleiden.nl, 200); Glottolog ref 575793 = 'Matthias Pache 2018, Contributions to Chibchan Historical Linguistics'. copies we hold lines 18501-18503 and PDF page index 470 (printed p. 449, checked with PyMuPDF) carry the quote verbatim, inside section 2.3.19 'Nutabe and other extinct Chibchan languages of the Cauca valley' (pp. 447-451), which is explicitly about Rivet 1943a's Nutabe (N) and old Chibchan Catio (K) = Glottolog anti1242; fn. 57 separates modern Embera-Catio (Chocoan). Rivet 1943: 25-26 held by the project shows the accented forms (amajú, taná, amiquiá, guare mé, otocaró, nacú, tobé) all with the mark on…
new_statements.relation_note: Grapheme-based vowel and consonant tables for Nutabe (Tables 58-59), the one suprasegmental remark quoted, and Proto-Chibchan > Nutabe sound correspondences for five words.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Where the colonial-era Nutabe/Old Catío forms carry a written accent, it is always on the final syllable (e.g. tobé 'old man', nacú 'salt', guacú 'old woman', otokaró 'chicken', amiquiá, K amajú); Pache reads this, conditionally, as final stress.
new_statements.exceptions: The circumflex in <tanâ> 'egg' is unexplained (possibly length or nasality); glide readings of <i>, <u>, <gu> are 'purely tentative'. Many forms carry no accent mark at all (ni, quia, ur, napa, tebuna).
new_statements.identity_note: Section is explicitly on Nutabe and the old (Chibchan) Catío of Rivet 1943a: 25-26, i.e. exactly Glottolog anti1242 'Antioquian'; Pache's fn. 57 separates them from modern Emberá-Catío (Chocoan). Glottolog lists the thesis (575793) but does not attach it to anti1242.

sources.note: Nothing. The whole Nutabé (N) / old Katio (K) corpus is ~40 words and phrases copied from Vázquez de Espinosa, Fr. Simón and Robledo (pp. 25-26), followed by Chibchan cognate sets (pp. 27-30) and ethnohistorical localisation (pp. 30-37). p. 30: 'Il y a peu à tirer, au point de vue grammatical, des vocabulaires nutabé et katío que je viens de reproduire.' The words accent/tonique/syllabe do not occur in pp. 25-39. The PDF itself is behind an altcha challenge; text was taken from Persée's per-page views.
